why: A verb outside the frozen surface is refused rather than guessed at.
A bound is never defaulted; the refusal names the flag that was omitted.
An argument this binary does not define is refused by name rather than ignored.

R11: a literal address only. Resolving a name is a network effect this binary does not take. Every bound is supplied so the run reaches the bind check rather than refusing earlier for a different reason.
A service verb without its registration path is an argument refusal, not an empty observation.

The product cut, executed. The host is really composed and really bound, the run window elapses, and the exit is the host's own ApiHostExit rendered by render_exit rather than a literal. The bind is EPHEMERAL on purpose: with :0 the requested and observed addresses differ, which is the only input under which a receipt that echoed the requested one can be caught. stdout stays exactly one JSON object -- the ready receipt is a durable artifact under the settled receipt root, not a second line here.

serve accepted --registration, --slot and --instance and never read one of them, which is the same defect reject_unknown exists to prevent from the other side. serve takes no registration at E1a, so the three are gone from its flag set and an operator who passes one is told so by name instead of being ignored.

The one bound this crate owns is not laxer than the bounds it borrows: ShutdownDrainAllowance refuses Duration::ZERO and so does ServeWindow. A host asked to serve for no time at all is a different verb, and the refusal names the flag.

The first of E1a's two shipped verbs to be exercised through a SUCCESSFUL run. status computes a three-way observation, and the receipt must carry which of the three it saw: an absent slot is empty, and it names no owner at all rather than an empty one. The registration path is a placeholder the validator resolves to a path outside the repository -- a committed fixture would move the direct-include inventory and a file written under a candidate tree voids a battery.

The pair to the row above, and the reason both exist: bytes that are not a registration record are UNREADABLE, never empty. Rendered from the outcome label alone these two runs were byte-identical on stdout, stderr and exit code, so an operator could not tell a free slot from a corrupt one. Comparing them here is what makes a rendering that collapses the two states fail.
